summary: ACP keeps the regulated roles where they already are: the merchant is merchant of record and system of record for orders, payments, taxes and compliance, and the PSP handles card data. That makes card rules, PCI DSS, strong customer authentication and consumer-protection law apply much as they do to any card-not-present sale. The open questions are about the agent. Does a buyer confirmation in an AI interface count as consent for liability rules, how do AI transparency rules apply to the surface, and how much buyer data does the agent pass on? Rows are dated; check each source before you rely on it.

rows.text: The merchant is merchant of record and handles refunds and chargebacks. For card purchases, Regulation Z limits unauthorized use to use without actual, implied or apparent authority, capped at the lesser of $50 or the amount before notice. Whether an agent acting outside the buyer's intent has apparent authority is untested.

For debit cards, Regulation E excludes transfers by someone the consumer gave the access device to until the consumer gives notice, which may leave a buyer liable for an agent it equipped with a credential.

In Amazon v. Perplexity (Ninth Circuit, 2026-08-04) the court vacated an injunction against an agentic browser, reasoning on its record that the user, not the agent vendor, accesses the site. The holding is limited to that record.
ACP has no KYC or sanctions layer. Screening sits with the merchant and its PSP, as in any card-not-present sale; OFAC obligations are unchanged.

California's CCPA regulations on automated decisionmaking technology took effect 2026-01-01; a business that uses ADMT for a significant decision about a consumer must comply by 2027-01-01 (11 CCR section 7200). The text lists financial or lending services, housing, education, employment and healthcare as significant decisions. Checkout shares buyer contact data, addresses and optional risk signals such as IP address and device fingerprint with the merchant.

As of 2026-10-20 a Federal Register search of CFPB documents since 2025-01-01 for 'artificial intelligence' and agent returned no rule or proposal specific to AI shopping agents. The search covers CFPB documents only, and a full-text search can miss other wording.

PSD2 SCA requires two factors and dynamic linking of amount and payee for remote payments. ACP's path is 3DS2 through authentication_required, Delegate Authentication and authentication_result; the spec names no regulation.
PSD2 bases payer liability on consent to the specific transaction. A buyer confirmation in an agent interface, without a signed record, is untested evidence of that consent.

AI Act Article 50(1) applies from 2026-08-02: providers of AI systems meant to interact directly with people must design them so people know they deal with an AI, unless that is obvious. That duty concerns the agent surface, not the merchant API. Generative systems on the market before that date have until 2026-12-02 for the Article 50(2) marking duty. The Digital Omnibus moved Annex III high-risk duties to 2027-12-02; a shopping agent is not high-risk by default.

GDPR applies to buyer data passed in checkout and to marketing consent. ACP records opt-ins through marketing_consent_options and marketing_consents; its marketing consent RFC cites GDPR, CAN-SPAM and CCPA as reasons for explicit consent but assigns no GDPR role to any party.

PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation reached provisional agreement on 2025-11-27; as of 2026-10-19 the Legislative Observatory listed both files as awaiting the Council's first-reading position, with no Official Journal publication. Readiness guides report no agent-specific provisions.

The Payment Services Regulations 2017 treat a payment as authorized only with the payer's consent (regulation 67). HM Treasury consulted from 2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06 on how consent and liability should adapt for agentic payments.

The FCA said on 2026-03-25 it will consider with HM Treasury whether rules must change for agentic AI payments. Regulation 100 of the Payment Services Regulations 2017 requires strong customer authentication when a payer initiates an electronic remote payment, with dynamic linking to amount and payee, subject to exemptions in the technical standards. ACP's 3DS2 path is how a merchant's PSP can apply it.
The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 amends UK GDPR rules on automated decision-making.

A web search on 2026-10-20 found no Canadian payment liability rule specific to AI agents. Stripe SPTs are available in Canada, and the Retail Payment Activities Act's risk management and funds safeguarding requirements have applied to payment service providers since 2025-09-08.
PIPEDA governs the personal information merchants and agent platforms exchange in checkout.
The MAS E-Payments User Protection Guidelines allocate liability for unauthorized e-payments. Stripe lists SPT availability for the US, Canada and listed European countries.
MAS issued AI risk management guidelines on 2026-10-07, effective 2027-10-07, naming agentic AI systems.

Visa's rules (since 2025-10-18) set requirements for Agentic Payment Providers. Visa defines one as the provider of an app that a cardholder uses to carry out tasks on the cardholder's behalf and that meets all of the following conditions. It can search, discover and buy once it receives the cardholder's payment instruction and verification, can undertake an Agentic Transaction, and can be used at more than one merchant. It transmits an EMV payment token, which it also stores when it pays with a stored credential, and passes that token to the merchant to complete the purchase through the merchant's acquirer. It takes no part in authorization, clearing or settlement. Whether a given ACP agent qualifies depends on those conditions.

Visa's rules govern Visa and its member institutions and yield to applicable law. A provider that qualifies must enroll in Visa Intelligent Commerce and register with Visa, directly or via an Agentic Payment Enabler. Within Visa's system, the cardholder is then responsible for its actions in an Agentic Transaction as if the cardholder had initiated it.

Visa calls none of its agent rules a liability shift and adds no agent-specific dispute condition or fee; its April 2026 US interchange schedule has no agentic category. It does require issuers to pay for Agentic Transactions made under a cardholder's payment instructions and not to block them wholesale. From 2026-10-24 it also accepts an Agentic Payment Provider's login ID among the evidence that can defeat a card-absent fraud dispute. Worldpay said on 2026-07-30 that no liability shift exists yet. ACP card payments otherwise follow existing card rules.

Mastercard says standard chargeback rights apply to agentic transactions. The 2026-06-02 Mastercard Rules add no agent-specific liability rule. They require pass-through wallet operators and checkout facilitators in Agent Pay to follow the Mastercard Agent Pay Program Standards. A web search on 2026-10-19 found no public copy of those standards.
PCI DSS: OpenAI reserves direct Delegate Payment integration for PSPs and PCI DSS Level 1 merchants and may require an attestation of compliance; feed and checkout specs carry no cardholder data.
EMVCo published a draft agentic payments framework on 2026-09-01 with Know Your Agent listed as possible future work; ACP itself has no agent registration.

OpenAI's commerce policy excludes products such as adult content, alcohol, nicotine, gambling, weapons and prescription-only medicines from ChatGPT shopping; ACP itself has age_verification_required and region_restricted message codes.
